headline: Kartogenin
punch: Right idea, wrong tissue, and possibly the wrong molecule.

headline: What it actually is
body: A small molecule that drives mesenchymal stem cells down the chondrogenic path. It works by disrupting the filamin A and **CBFβ** interaction, freeing CBFβ to partner with **RUNX1**, which turns on cartilage genes including **SOX9**. | It also feeds TGF-β and SMAD signalling. In cell work it has an **EC50 of 100 nM** and it has been called a game changer for cartilage regeneration.
punch: It turns stem cells into cartilage cells.

headline: It genuinely works
body: The preclinical record is real. It promotes proliferation and chondrogenic differentiation of MSCs, repairs osteoarthritic lesions in mouse models, and prevents matrix loss. | Mechanistically it raises the number of CD44 and CD105 positive stem cells and acts through PI3K-Akt. For articular cartilage repair this is a well-supported compound with a clear target.

headline: The tissue is wrong
subhead: DOWNSIDE · WHAT IT WAS TESTED ON
body: Almost every efficacy study is **articular cartilage repair**, meaning the smooth cartilage on the ends of bones inside a joint. That is a different tissue from the growth plate with a different job. | Articular cartilage is meant to stay cartilage permanently. Growth plate cartilage is meant to proliferate, hypertrophy and be replaced by bone. A drug that makes stable articular cartilage is not obviously a drug that lengthens bone.
punch: ==Joint cartilage and growth plate are not the same tissue.==

headline: The delivery is wrong
body: The research delivery route is overwhelmingly **intra-articular**, injected directly into a joint, and a whole literature exists on nanocarrier systems built specifically to keep it there. | That tells you something: the compound is being engineered for local retention because getting it to a target tissue systemically is the hard part. A joint is a space you can inject into. A growth plate is not.
punch: The route the research uses is not available here.

headline: It may be a prodrug
body: This is the result that should change how anyone thinks about it. After oral or intra-articular dosing in mice, the group measured what was actually present in cartilage by mass spectrometry. | Oral and intra-articular delivery both improved osteoarthritis, but **only 4-ABP was detectable in cartilage**, not kartogenin itself. 4-ABP alone induced MSC chondrogenesis and repaired lesions.
punch: The thing reaching the tissue was the metabolite.

headline: Which raises a question
body: If the active species at the tissue is the metabolite rather than the parent, then dosing, route and formulation decisions made about kartogenin are decisions about a delivery vehicle, not about the drug. | That is not a reason to dismiss it. It is a reason to be precise that the evidence supports a metabolite reaching cartilage, and that the parent was not found there.
punch: Measure what arrives, not what you injected.

headline: Sublingual is worse
body: One specific thing worth knowing, because it runs opposite to the usual intuition. Kartogenin carries a carboxylic acid group, and at oral mucosal pH around 6.8 to 7.2 that group is almost entirely ionised. | Ionised molecules cross membranes badly. So sublingual delivery is reasoned to be pharmacokinetically **worse** than swallowing it, which inverts the advantage sublingual usually has.
punch: The usual sublingual trick fails on this one.

headline: No growth plate data
body: There is no study of kartogenin on growth plate chondrocytes specifically, no longitudinal bone growth endpoint, and no human pharmacokinetic data at all. | Of kartogenin, liquiritigenin and pregnenolone, pregnenolone is the only one with actual human PK, and even that is limited. This compound has none.
punch: No human PK. No growth plate study. None.

headline: Verdict
body: A real compound with a clean mechanism and genuine preclinical support, for a different tissue, by a route you cannot use, with the active species at the target possibly being its metabolite. | The chondrogenic logic is attractive and that is exactly why it needs stating plainly: nothing here was measured on a growth plate, in a human, or at a dose anyone can reproduce.
punch: Good molecule. No evidence for this use.
